questions.q: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. Find the probability their sum is $8$.
How many ways can a committee of $4$ be chosen from $10$ people?
questions.answer: Order doesn't matter, so use combinations: $\binom{10}{4}=\dfrac{10!}{4!\,6!}=\dfrac{10\cdot9\cdot8\cdot7}{4\cdot3\cdot2\cdot1}=210$.

questions.q: How many ways can $2$ officers (president, vice president — order matters) be chosen from $6$ candidates?
Explain, using Theorem 6.1, how $\binom{6}{2}$ relates to $P(6,2)$ from the previous question.
questions.answer: Theorem 6.1 says $\binom{6}{2}=\dfrac{P(6,2)}{2!}=\dfrac{30}{2}=15$ — combinations undercount permutations by exactly the $2!$ orderings of each chosen pair.
